rhymes.content:
ರೊಟ್ಟಿ ಅಂಗಡಿ ಕಿಟ್ಟಿಪ್ಪ
ನಂಗಂದು ರೊಟ್ಟಿ ತಟ್ಟಿಪ್ಪ

ಒಂಭತ್ತು ಕಾಸಿಗೆ ತಟ್ಟಿಪ್ಪ
ಬಿಟ್ಟಿ ಹೋಗೆನು ಕಿಟ್ಟಿಪ್ಪ

ರೊಟ್ಟಿ ಅಂಗಡಿ ಕಿಟ್ಟಿಪ್ಪ
ರೊಟ್ಟಿಯ ನೋಡಿ ತಟ್ಟಿಪ್ಪ
ರೊಟ್ಟಿಯ ಸುತ್ತು ಹಸಿ ಹಸಿ ಹಿಟ್ಟಿ
ರೊಟ್ಟಿಯ ಬೇರೆ ತಟ್ಟಿಪ್ಪ
ನನಗಿದು ಬೇಡ ಕಿಟ್ಟಿಪ್ಪ

rhymes.title: My Eyes are Windows
rhymes.content:
My eyes are windows, through which I look and see
The Sunshine in the garden
And blossom on the tree
I must try with all my might
To keep my windows
Clean and bright

rhymes.title: Two Lovely Eyes
rhymes.content:
Two lovely eyes,
Help me to see.
Two lovely ears,
help me to hear.
One lovely nose,
Helps me to smell.
One little mouth,
To talk and tell.
Two long hands,
To write, paint and work.
Two strong legs,
To hop, skip and jump.
Thank you, God, for this body of mine,
Fit and healthy and oh! So fine.

rhymes.title: Body Parts
rhymes.content:
My hands are for clapping,
My arms can hug tight.
My fingers can snap,
Or can turn out tight.
My legs are for jumping,
My eyes help me see.
This is my body,
And I love all of me.

rhymes.title: Days of the Week
rhymes.content:
Every week has seven days,
seven days, seven days.
I pray on Monday.
I walk on Tuesday.
I talk on Wednesday.
I dance on Thursday.
I have fun on Friday.
I swim on Saturday.
Stop, stop, it is Sunday
Enjoy one day holiday.

rhymes.title: Values for Me
rhymes.content:
I am special, I am kind,
I use my heart, and my mind.
I tell the truth and always share,
with my friends for whom I care.
Helping others, doing right,
Makes my heart feel big and bright!
I have values, that is true,
And so do all my friends I knew!

shloka.sanskrit:
Brahma Murāri Surārchita Liṅgam
Nirmala Bhāṣita Śobhita Liṅgam
Janmaja Duḥkha Vināśaka Liṅgam
Tat Praṇamāmi Sadāśiva Liṅgam

Deva Muni Pravarārchita Liṅgam
Kāma Dahana Karuṇākara Liṅgam
Rāvaṇa Darpa Vināśaka Liṅgam
Tat Praṇamāmi Sadāśiva Liṅgam
shloka.transliteration:
Brahma Murāri Surārchita Liṅgam
Nirmala Bhāṣita Śobhita Liṅgam
Janmaja Duḥkha Vināśaka Liṅgam
Tat Praṇamāmi Sadāśiva Liṅgam

Deva Muni Pravarārchita Liṅgam
Kāma Dahana Karuṇākara Liṅgam
Rāvaṇa Darpa Vināśaka Liṅgam
Tat Praṇamāmi Sadāśiva Liṅgam
shloka.meaning: I bow before that Sada Shiva Linga, which is worshipped by Brahma, Vishnu and other Gods, which is praised by pure and holy speeches, and which destroys the cycle of births and deaths.

story.title: The Elves and the Shoemaker
story.content:
Once upon a time, there was a kind shoemaker who lived in a small house with his wife. They worked hard every day making shoes, but they were very poor. They didn’t have enough money to buy food, and soon they didn’t even have enough leather to make shoes.

One evening, after a long day of work, the shoemaker sighed. "I wish we had enough money to buy more leather and make more shoes," he said. "But I don’t know how we will manage."

That night, the shoemaker and his wife went to bed early, feeling sad. But little did they know, something magical was about to happen.

When the shoemaker woke up the next morning, he saw something amazing! On his workbench were beautifully made shoes, shining and perfect. He couldn't believe his eyes! The shoes were ready to be sold, and the shoemaker was so happy.

He decided to sell the shoes in the market, and guess what? The shoes sold for a lot of money! The shoemaker bought more leather, hoping to make even more shoes. But that night, something even more magical happened.

When he woke up the next morning, more shoes had been made while he was sleeping! They were just as perfect as the first pair. The shoemaker couldn’t understand who was helping him, but he was very grateful.

Night after night, this continued. Every morning, the shoemaker would wake up to find more beautiful shoes made while he slept.

One evening, the shoemaker and his wife decided to stay awake and find out who was making the shoes. So, they hid behind a curtain and waited.

To their surprise, in the middle of the night, two tiny elves appeared. The elves worked quickly, sewing and stitching the shoes, and soon they were done. Then, the little elves quietly disappeared into the night.

The shoemaker was so happy! The next day, he made tiny clothes for the elves as a thank you. That night, when the elves came to help, the shoemaker and his wife gave the clothes to them.

The elves were very happy and said, “Thank you! We are so glad you gave us clothes. Now we will help you even more!”

From that day on, the elves and the shoemaker worked together, and the shoemaker’s shop became the most famous one in the land.

And they all lived happily ever after.
story.moral: Kindness and hard work are always rewarded.
